title: Five Hua Hin-area hotels recognised among 71 across Thailand
desc: Five Hua Hin-area hotels recognised among 71 across Thailand Legacy Five hotels in and around Hua Hin have been recognised in the Michelin Guide’s 2026 hotel selection , with two properties receiving the distinction for the first time as Thailand’s total number of recognised hotels increases to 71. The results, announced previously on September 18, highlight the coastal destination’s presence in the country’s hospitality sector. All five properties received One Michelin Key, which is awarded to hotels offering what Michelin describes as a very special stay. The number of Hua Hin Michelin Key hotels has increased as part of a wider expansion of the awards across Thailand, with the national total rising from 62 properties in 2025 to 71 this year. The 2026 selection includes six Three-Key hotels, 22 Two-Key hotels and 43 One-Key hotels. Among the two newcomers are Chiva-Som Hua Hin, a wellness retreat , and Devasom Hua Hin, a boutique beachfront resort near Cha-am. Both were included in the Michelin Key selection for the first time. They join three previously recognised properties: Anantara Hua Hin Resort & Spa, V Villas Hua Hin and Aleenta Resort & Spa

title_cn: 泰国政府启动洪灾救济金发放
summary_cn: 泰国政府已开始发放首批洪灾救济金。灾难预防与减灾部门表示，超过142万户家庭通过Tang Rat应用程序注册申请救济。政府通过该应用平台推进救济发放工作，旨在为洪灾受害者提供及时的财政支援，帮助灾区居民尽快恢复正常生活。
desc_original: Authorities on Thursday began transferring the first flood relief payments, as more than 1.42 million households have registered for assistance through the Tang Rat app, the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation (DDPM) said.

title: MRTA opens properties to investment
desc: The Mass Rapid Transit Authority of Thailand (MRTA) plans to develop nearly 70 sites to generate more revenue and make better use of its land, with the first major project planned for the Rama IX area.
title_cn: 曼谷捷运局开放70个地块投资开发
summary_cn: 泰国大众快速运输局（MRTA）计划开发近70个地块以增加收入，并更好地利用其地产资源。首个重大项目位于拉玛九世（Rama IX）地区。此举将为投资者创造商业机会，同时增加公共运输部门的财政收入，推动曼谷的房地产和基础设施发展。
desc_original: The Mass Rapid Transit Authority of Thailand (MRTA) plans to develop nearly 70 sites to generate more revenue and make better use of its land, with the first major project planned for the Rama IX area.

title: Govt defends  transfer of district chief
desc: Deputy Interior Minister Polapee Suwunchwee has defended the transfer of Ban Sang district chief Setthawut Wonglerwut, saying the decision was based on reports from provincial officials and local leaders rather than political pressure.
title_cn: 政府为班桑县县长调任辩护
summary_cn: 泰国副内政部长普拉佩·苏温楚威为班桑县（Ban Sang）县长塞塔武特·翁勒卖的调任辩护，强调该决定基于省级官员和地方领导人的报告，而非政治压力。
desc_original: Deputy Interior Minister Polapee Suwunchwee has defended the transfer of Ban Sang district chief Setthawut Wonglerwut, saying the decision was based on reports from provincial officials and local leaders rather than political pressure.

title: Working groups to draw up 'open government' plans
desc: Four working groups will develop proposals on corruption, environmental problems, public participation and access to justice as Thailand works on its next national action plan for open government.
title_cn: 泰国组建工作组制定「开放政府」计划
summary_cn: 泰国成立四个工作小组，分别针对腐败、环保问题、公众参与和司法正义四个领域制定建议书，为制定下一阶段国家开放政府行动计划做准备，推进政府透明度和问责制建设。
desc_original: Four working groups will develop proposals on corruption, environmental problems, public participation and access to justice as Thailand works on its next national action plan for open government.

title: Sri Lanka woos Thais ahead of 2027 expo
desc: Sri Lanka is seeking Thai investment and business partnerships in sectors ranging from food and manufacturing to technology, tourism and healthcare as it prepares for Sri Lanka Expo 2027 in Colombo.

title: Thailand weather today, 9 October: heavy rain in 16 provinces, Bangkok a few showers
desc: Thailand weather today, 9 October: heavy rain in 16 provinces, Bangkok a few showers Legacy The Thai Meteorological Department forecasts heavy rain in 16 provinces today, with the Northeast, East and South hit hardest. Amnat Charoen, Bueng Kan, Nakhon Phanom, Si Sa Ket, Surin and Ubon Ratchathani face isolated heavy rain, along with Chanthaburi and Trat in the East. The South also sees heavy rain across Nakhon Si Thammarat, Narathiwat, Phatthalung, Phetchaburi, Prachuap Khiri Khan, Songkhla, Surat Thani and Yala. Bangkok can expect isolated thundershowers, with lows of 25°C and highs of 35°C. Residents in affected areas are warned of flash floods and overflows, particularly along waterways near foothills and in low-lying land. A high-pressure system covers the upper North and upper Northeast. Southeasterly winds carry moisture from the South China Sea into the eastern Northeast and the East. A monsoon trough lies across the Gulf and the South, driving the wet conditions there. Bangkok The capital sees isolated thundershowers through the forecast period. Lows of 25°C and highs of 35°C are expected, with northeasterly winds of 10 to 20km/h. North Isolated thundershowers are forecast

title: Thai candy floss wrapped mid-flight draws Peking duck jokes
desc: Thai candy floss wrapped mid-flight draws Peking duck jokes Legacy A passenger enjoying Thailand’s traditional sweet treat , roti sai mai, during a flight has attracted attention online after another traveller jokingly compared the dessert to Peking duck wraps . The encounter was shared on Threads on October 5 by a model using the account @runqianlin , who filmed a fellow passenger preparing the snack on board an aircraft. In a Chinese-language caption, the model joked that someone appeared to be rolling Peking duck wraps during the flight and asked whether they could have some. However, the passenger was not preparing the famous Chinese dish. The food appeared to be roti sai mai, a traditional Thai dessert made by wrapping fine strands of spun sugar in thin, soft roti sheets. The footage showed the passenger handling a pale green roti sheet with candy floss in the middle, ready to be rolled and eaten. title: 2 Thai men arrested after body found in burned pickup in Trang
desc: 2 Thai men arrested after body found in burned pickup in Trang Legacy Police in Trang arrested two Thai men after a man was found dead inside a burned-out pickup truck near Tha Ngio Reservoir in Huai Yot district. The case is linked to a dispute over a drug deal. Firefighters were called to a roadside forest near the reservoir on the night of October 6 after a pickup truck was found on fire. Once the fire was extinguished, firefighters discovered human remains inside the vehicle. A Thai woman, Siriluck, contacted Huai Yot Police Station after seeing a rescue foundation post and a news report showing the vehicle’s registration. She believed the deceased was her 37 year old brother, Theerasak, from Sichon district in Nakhon Si Thammarat. Siriluck said she had been unable to contact her brother for several days. She said Theerasak worked tapping rubber with his partner and travelled between Bang Klam and Sichon, where their mother lived alone following their father’s death. She said she could not understand why her brother would have gone to the reservoir. desc: Phuket rider says hotel staff eat food delivered to foreign guest at reception Legacy A food delivery rider in Phuket filed a police complaint, alleging that hotel staff took and ate fried chicken he had delivered for a foreign guest. The rider, who has not been identified, shared his account with the Phuket Times Facebook page on October 7. He also did not disclose the name of the hotel involved. According to the rider, he accepted an order for fried chicken and left the food at the hotel’s reception counter. He said delivery riders were normally instructed to leave food at reception rather than taking orders directly to guests’ rooms. The rider said he left the hotel to collect his next delivery. He later received a complaint from the customer through the delivery application’s reporting system, stating that the food had not arrived. title: Bangkok readies flood defences for IMF-World Bank meetings
desc: Bangkok readies flood defences for IMF-World Bank meetings Legacy Bangkok is preparing drainage crews, mobile pumps and emergency response measures around venues for the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings 2026 from October 12 to 16. Surapong Sarapa, director of the Meteorological Department’s Weather Forecast Division, said yesterday, October 7, that weather conditions would remain unsettled on October 10 and 11 as Thailand moves from the end of the rainy season into the start of winter. Rainfall during those two days is expected to reach around 30 to 50 millimetres, with periods of heavy rain lasting for relatively short periods. Surapong said rainfall should then return to more normal levels during the period covering the IMF-World Bank meetings. Bangkok’s Department of Drainage and Sewerage has prepared additional flood prevention measures around the meeting area. Photo via Ministry of Finance The department said water from roads would be pumped directly into Saen Saep Canal before being discharged through Khlong Tan and Phadung Krung Kasem Canal into the Chao Phraya River. Water collection facilities surrounding the meeting area will also be used to pump water from Saen Saep Canal

summary_cn: 泰国近期洪灾预计将对第四季度国内汽车销售造成轻微影响。消费者因灾情延迟购车计划，汽车经销商面临交付延误问题。根据泰国马自达销售公司预测，灾害天气状况将持续对车市购销活动构成压力。

summary_cn: 泰国财政部正起草新的投资促进法，拟用以替代泰国工业委员会（Board of Investment，BoI）目前实施的税收优惠政策。新法案旨在创新投资激励机制，为国内外投资者提供更优化的政策环境，进一步推动泰国经济投资吸引力。
desc_original: The Revenue Department is drafting a new investment promotion law to replace the tax incentives currently provided by the Board of Investment (BoI).

desc: The Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) index is expected to finish at 1,680 points by year-end, supported by investment in artificial intelligence (AI) technology and its supply chain, listed-company earnings, foreign fund inflows and a recovery in the domestic economy, says the Investment Analysts Association (IAA).

summary_cn: 泰国投资分析师协会预测，证券交易所（SET）指数有望在今年年底达到1680点。市场支撑因素包括人工智能及其供应链领域的投资增加、上市公司业绩改善、外资基金持续流入以及国内经济复苏。

desc: The insurance industry is reporting more complex cyberthreats powered by artificial intelligence (AI), prompting the Office of the Insurance Commission (OIC) to join hands with 67 life and non-life insurers to strengthen cyber-resilience, from prevention and response to recovery.

summary_cn: 泰国保险业面临人工智能驱动的复杂网络威胁。保险监管委员会（OIC）联合67家寿险及产险公司，从预防、应对到恢复等全环节强化网络防护能力，提升行业网络韧性。

title: Oil Fuel Fund mulls loan options
desc: The Energy Ministry has stressed that borrowing money from banks to shore up the loss-riddled Oil Fuel Fund is a last resort, despite the fund's deficit approaching 100 billion baht.
title_cn: 石油燃料基金探索银行融资方案
summary_cn: 泰国石油燃料基金长期亏损，赤字已接近100亿泰铢。能源部强调向银行借贷是最后手段，基金面临严峻财务困难。政府正研究其他救助融资方案以度过难关。
desc_original: The Energy Ministry has stressed that borrowing money from banks to shore up the loss-riddled Oil Fuel Fund is a last resort, despite the fund's deficit approaching 100 billion baht.

title: Panel seeks to beef up flood preparedness
desc: A private sector panel is preparing a letter to the prime minister urging the government to accelerate efforts to strengthen Thailand's preparedness for future flooding.
title_cn: 民营部门敦促政府加强防洪准备工作
summary_cn: 泰国民营部门正准备致函总理，敦促政府加速推进防洪准备工作。近期严重洪灾凸显国家防灾体系薄弱，业界呼吁政府采取更有力、更前瞻的防灾措施。
desc_original: A private sector panel is preparing a letter to the prime minister urging the government to accelerate efforts to strengthen Thailand's preparedness for future flooding.

title: Bangkok faces submersion risk
desc: Bangkok could have as much as one-third of its area permanently submerged by 2050 if the government fails to overhaul the country's water-management system and take more aggressive action on climate change, environmental and water-management experts warned at a forum.
title_cn: 曼谷面临沉没风险
summary_cn: 环保人士警告，若政府不能改革水资源管理系统、加强气候行动，曼谷到2050年可能有三分之一的区域被永久沉没。这涉及泰国首都的未来发展和防灾规划。
desc_original: Bangkok could have as much as one-third of its area permanently submerged by 2050 if the government fails to overhaul the country's water-management system and take more aggressive action on climate change, environmental and water-management experts warned at a forum.

desc_original: One Flag Thailand has completed its first world-record mission, flying a 4,303-square-foot Thai national flag over Pattaya.

title: ThaiHealth funding debate heats up

desc_original: The government's plan to end ThaiHealth's earmarked alcohol and tobacco tax funding of more than 4 billion baht a year has drawn mixed views over fiscal scrutiny, independence and public health.

title: Govt moves to protect meet
desc: The government has developed a business continuity plan to ensure the 2026 IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings run smoothly, even if heavy rainfall mars the global gathering, said Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas.

desc_original: The government has developed a business continuity plan to ensure the 2026 IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings run smoothly, even if heavy rainfall mars the global gathering, said Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas.

title: Fighter jet tyre bursts on Ubon runway, diverts Bangkok flights
desc: Fighter jet tyre bursts on Ubon runway, diverts Bangkok flights Legacy An F-5 TH fighter jet suffered a tyre blowout while landing at Ubon Ratchathani Airport today, October 7, temporarily closing the runway and forcing some passenger flights from Bangkok to turn back . The Royal Thai Air Force said the aircraft, operated by Squadron 211 of Wing 21 in Ubon Ratchathani, developed the problem on the runway at around 11.30am. The incident affected incoming commercial flights while airport staff worked to move the disabled aircraft and clear the runway. Among the affected services were AirAsia flight FD3374 from Don Mueang to Ubon Ratchathani and Thai VietJet flight VZ220 from Suvarnabhumi to Ubon Ratchathani. Photo via ป้อนป้อนพาเที่ยว Both were among the flights unable to land while the runway was closed for safety reasons and had to return to Bangkok. The Air Force said the problem was caused by one of the fighter jet’s tyres bursting during landing. It added that this type of failure can occur with aircraft and may be caused by a wheel hitting an object or other foreign material on the runway during touchdown. Airport rescue personnel and other relevant teams immediately inspected

title: 27 provinces, Bangkok remain flooded as crisis continues
desc: 27 provinces, Bangkok remain flooded as crisis continues Legacy Flooding remains across 27 provinces and Bangkok , affecting more than 3.16 million people and leaving 52 dead as heavy rain and runoff from northern Thailand continue to worsen conditions across central and eastern regions. The Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation (DDPM) said at 6am today, October 7, that floods were affecting 123 districts, 984 subdistricts and 7,215 villages, covering 1,154,875 households and 3,160,972 people. The affected provinces are Mae Hong Son, Chiang Mai, Lamphun, Nan, Phayao, Tak, Nakhon Sawan, Uthai Thani, Lop Buri, Sing Buri, Chai Nat, Suphan Buri, Kanchanaburi, Ang Thong, Saraburi, Ayutthaya, Samut Prakan, Pathum Thani, Nakhon Pathom, Ratchaburi, Samut Songkhram, Phetchaburi, Nakhon Nayok, Prachin Buri, Chachoengsao, Chon Buri and Rayong, along with Bangkok. Photo via JS100 Radio Prachin Buri recorded the highest death toll, with 19 people killed and 59,934 households affected across all seven districts. Water levels there were still rising. title: Your health insurance may not give you the specialist you want
desc: Your health insurance may not give you the specialist you want Legacy At many private hospitals in Thailand, choosing a specialist is easier than working out what your outpatient insurance will pay for. The online appointment system gives patients two options: ask the hospital to recommend a doctor or choose the doctor yourself. Some hospitals also let patients search by speciality, language and preferred date, with instant booking available for some doctors. For an expat using Thailand’s private healthcare system, finding the right specialist is usually straightforward; the insurance side is less obvious. Being free to book a cardiologist, neurologist or orthopaedic specialist does not mean your policy will pay for that consultation in the way you expect. The answer can depend on whether the appointment counts as outpatient care, how the provider is paid and what happens if the first consultation leads to scans, procedures or hospital treatment. desc: Around 2,000 pigs drown in Prachin Buri farm floods Legacy Around 2,000 pigs drowned after flash floods hit a large farm in Prachin Buri, prompting livestock officials to deploy more than 50 staff and heavy machinery to remove and bury the carcasses . title: Phuket launches Licence Lab to help small stays get licensed
desc: Phuket launches Licence Lab to help small stays get licensed Legacy Phuket has launched the “ Phuket Licence Lab ” to help small and medium-sized accommodation businesses overcome building and regulatory problems that have prevented many from obtaining the licences needed to operate legally . Five organisations from the professional, academic and tourism sectors signed a memorandum of understanding for the project on October 5 at Phuket City Development Company, or PKCD, in Mueang Phuket district. The project was developed because many small and medium-sized accommodation businesses in Phuket remain unable to obtain licences, often because their buildings were constructed before certain regulations came into force. Common obstacles include fire exits, fire protection systems, building setbacks and open-space requirements, urban planning rules, wastewater treatment systems and land ownership documents. These problems can affect both guest safety and the ability of operators to bring their businesses into compliance. desc: GMM MUSIC เปิดผลประกอบการครึ่งปีแรก กวาดรายได้ 2,161.2 ล้านบาท โตขึ้น 12.2% กำไรสุทธิ 280.7 ล้านบาท เพิ่มขึ้น 29.2% สวนเศรษฐกิจซบ ย้ำเป็นธุรกิจหลักที่แข็งแกร่งของ GMM GRAMMY
title_cn: GMM Music 上半年利润暴增 29.2%
summary_cn: 泰国音乐娱乐公司 GMM Music（GMM GRAMMY 旗下）公布上半年财报：营收 21.61 亿泰铢，同比增长 12.2%；净利润 2.807 亿泰铢，增幅达 29.2%。音乐版权、艺人经纪和演艺活动成为核心增长动力。在经济整体疲软背景下，GMM Music 仍保持强劲盈利表现，成为集团的业绩支柱。
